established_findings.statement: Large language models (LLMs) and LLM-based multi-agent architectures are being actively applied to NetOps tasks such as intent-to-configuration translation, configuration/template synthesis, root-cause analysis, and automated remediation proposals.
limitations: Most studies evaluate in simulated or lab settings rather than production live networks
Task scopes differ across papers (intent translation, template synthesis, RCA), limiting direct comparability

established_findings.statement: LLM outputs for NetOps are prone to hallucination, misconfiguration, and adversarially induced actionable errors; targeted poisoning of retrieval context can substantially increase actionable misconfiguration rates in evaluated simulators.
limitations: Adversarial experiments reported in synthetic/simulated SOC/RAG settings; transferability to all NetOps pipelines not demonstrated
Severity metrics (e.g., "actionable misconfiguration rate") vary by study and attacker model

established_findings.statement: Operational reliability of LLM-enabled NetOps depends heavily on surrounding systems (validators, constraint encoders, canary/rollback procedures, tool-bounded workflows) rather than LLM generation alone.
limitations: These are synthesis and position works arguing dependency on surrounding machinery; quantitative effect sizes across diverse deployments are limited
Implementation specifics (which validators, how integrated) vary and are often only prototyped

established_findings.statement: Constraint-based adaptation, generate→validate→repair pipelines, and validator-assisted workflows improve LLM-based NetOps accuracy in reported studies and prototypes.
limitations: Reported improvements are study- and dataset-specific; generalization to broader workloads is not fully validated
Some works report human-in-the-loop or fine-tuning steps that affect measured accuracy

established_findings.statement: Standalone LLM self-correction (prompted LLMs correcting their own outputs) shows mixed/limited reliability; self-correction is more effective when using reliable external feedback or extensive fine-tuning/RL.
limitations: Improvements from RL/fine-tuning may require substantial compute and data, limiting practicality
Task-dependent: some tasks amenable to self-correction, others not

unresolved_questions.statement: Can LLM-driven agents safely and autonomously execute network configuration changes in production environments without human-in-the-loop oversight?
limitations: Reviews note weak production evidence; absence of production-scale controlled trials in supplied records
Answer depends on specific governance, rollback, and verification contracts not standardized

unresolved_questions.statement: What standardized, execution-oriented benchmark(s) effectively measure workflow-centred safety (generation + verification + simulated enactment + rollback) for agentic NetOps systems?
limitations: Several papers call for such benchmarks but do not provide a community-accepted, widely-adopted execution benchmark in the supplied records
Existing benchmarks (log/CTI/security) cover parts of the pipeline but not the full enactment+rollback lifecycle

unresolved_questions.statement: How robust are adversarial-defence techniques (e.g., provenance/uncertainty attestation) when applied specifically to NetOps RAG pipelines under realistic threat models?
limitations: Defenses demonstrated for SOC/RAG simulators; direct NetOps-targeted evaluations limited in supplied records
Effectiveness depends on retrieval corpus properties and attacker capabilities

unresolved_questions.statement: To what extent do public corpora of real-world network configurations exist and suffice for reproducible, large-scale evaluation of LLM-driven NetOps?
limitations: Some works build domain-specific corpora but indicate data scarcity and dataset construction effort
Representativeness of available corpora for diverse vendor setups/topologies is unclear

candidate_gaps.statement: There is a gap: no widely-adopted, execution-oriented NetOps benchmark combines LLM generation, formal/verifier checks, simulated enactment, and rollback-aware scoring.
limitations: Surveys call for such benchmarks but do not perform exhaustive search of every niche benchmark; possible small-scale proposals may exist outside supplied records
Building such a benchmark requires careful task formalization and simulator/verifier integration

candidate_gaps.statement: Public, diverse corpora of real-world multi-vendor network configurations suitable for large-scale LLM evaluation appear limited, necessitating dataset construction or curation efforts.
limitations: Some projects create domain corpora (so availability is not zero); gap refers to scale/diversity and community adoption
Legal/privacy constraints limit distribution of real operator configs

candidate_gaps.statement: Effectiveness limits of LLM self-correction for safety-critical NetOps remain an open research gap; existing self-correction methods often require external reliable signals or costly RL/fine-tuning.
limitations: Some task categories admit effective self-correction; gap concerns general, safety-critical NetOps tasks
Practicality trade-offs (compute, data) for RL/fine-tuning are context-dependent

excluded_claims: LLMs are currently production-ready to autonomously perform live network configuration changes across diverse, real-world networks without human oversight or external verification (unsupported by supplied records).

Standalone prompted LLM self-correction (without reliable external validators or substantial fine-tuning/RL) reliably eliminates hallucinations and misconfigurations in NetOps (contradicted by critical surveys and method papers).

There exists a community-accepted, execution-oriented benchmark demonstrating safe autonomous NetOps at production scale with statistical evidence of safety across vendors and topologies (no such benchmark found in supplied records).
